extraction.name: HELVIPAD
extraction.description: A real-world dataset for omnidirectional stereo depth estimation featuring about 40K video frames from diverse indoor and outdoor scenes under varied lighting conditions. It was collected with two 360° cameras in a top-bottom setup and a LiDAR sensor, and includes depth and disparity labels plus an augmented training set with increased label density via depth completion.
extraction.creator: Mehdi Zayene; Jannik Endres; Albias Havolli; Charles Corbiere; Salim Cherkaoui; Alexandre Kontouli; Alexandre Alahi
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected by recording video sequences in dynamic indoor and outdoor scenes across a university campus using a custom-built rig with two vertically arranged omnidirectional cameras synchronized with a LiDAR sensor; LiDAR point clouds were projected onto frames to obtain depth maps and disparity maps, and depth completion was later applied to augment training labels.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Missing/sparse depth labels were handled with depth completion, which interpolated missing values and removed out-of-distribution samples to increase label density.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw/source data consisted of omnidirectional video sequences (top and bottom images) synchronized with LiDAR point clouds, from which depth maps and disparity maps were produced.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Depth and disparity labels were generated automatically by projecting LiDAR point clouds onto equirectangular images, optimizing LiDAR-to-image alignment, and augmenting training labels with a fully automated depth completion pipeline using temporally aggregated point clouds, interpolation, and filtering.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper evaluates annotation quality by measuring LiDAR-image alignment error and validating the depth completion pipeline on held-out LiDAR points, reporting pixel error and label-density/error tradeoffs.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: One automatically generated depth/disparity label map per paired image frame, with original sparse labels covering about 12% of pixels and augmented labels covering about 61% of pixels.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: LiDAR-to-image mapping optimization using BFGS and an automated depth completion pipeline based on temporal aggregation, k-nearest-neighbor interpolation on spherical grids, and filtering were used to generate/augment labels.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may underrepresent some conditions and scene types, especially unseen or underrepresented situations such as outdoor scenes at night; models trained on specific environments generalize poorly outside those domains.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Depth labels are sparse without completion; the depth completion approach is limited for fast-moving objects like cars; LiDAR-camera occlusions were not explicitly handled; and indoor-trained models show limited generalization to outdoor and night scenes.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to support robotics and depth estimation research in dynamic human environments, with implications for safer deployment and robustness assessment in real-world settings.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Human presence/pedestrian activity and environmental context including indoor/outdoor location and lighting/time conditions (e.g., night) are captured.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Use cases include training, validation, testing, benchmarking, and robustness/generalization assessment for omnidirectional stereo depth estimation models; the augmented depth-completed labels are specifically used as training data augmentation.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Training data augmentation via depth completion to increase label density; temporal aggregation of point clouds from the current frame plus four preceding and four succeeding frames.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Projected LiDAR point clouds onto equirectangular images by applying initial rotation/translation, converting points to spherical coordinates, projecting to the equirectangular plane, and optimizing alignment with BFGS; depth completion pipeline interpolated depth on spherical grid points using k-nearest neighbors and filtered out points with high uncertainty or insufficient nearby measurements; cropped unnecessary sky and ground regions.

name.evidence: We introduce HELVIPAD, a real-world dataset for omnidirectional stereo depth estimation

description.evidence: We introduce HELVIPAD, a real-world dataset for omnidirectional stereo depth estimation, featuring 40K video frames from video sequences across diverse environments, including crowded indoor and outdoor scenes with various lighting conditions. Collected using two 360° cameras in a top-bottom setup and a LiDAR sensor, the dataset includes accurate depth and disparity labels... Additionally, we provide an augmented training set with an increased label density by using depth completion.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: we conduct a detailed scene-wise analysis to study each method’s ability to generalize to unseen or underrepresented situations, such as outdoor scenes at night.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Given the sparse nature of LiDAR point clouds compared to high-resolution camera images, ground-truth depth labels cover only a fraction of the total pixels... Note that this approach is limited for fast-moving objects like cars... Occlusions were not explicitly handled, as the small LiDAR-camera baseline minimizes their impact... indoor-trained models show a clear limitation in generalizing to outdoor scenes, particularly at night.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Mobile robots are increasingly used in real-world applications such as autonomous driving, healthcare, or agriculture, where accurate 3D representations of dynamic human environments are crucial for navigation and interaction... To safely deploy learning systems in real-world settings, it is essential to assess their ability to generalize to unseen or underrepresented conditions
